title: Low-Weight Canonical Logical Bases from Pair-Partition Codes
abstract: We construct complete canonical logical bases for qubit CSS codes by assigning quaternary coefficients to binary circulant permutation matrix pair-partition (CPM-PP) checks, constructing and normalizing logical representatives, and expanding the result into binary matrices. When the two check systems have invertible submatrices on disjoint column sets, cofactor representatives are canonically paired by the inverse of a single pairing polynomial. The resulting pairs span the entire logical space. When the pairing polynomial is a cyclic-shift monomial with coefficient one, normalization preserves the binary weights of the representatives. We state the construction for general block dimensions and CPM size, work through a corresponding example, and report the parameters, check ranks, and basis weights of seven binary codes. Representative examples have parameters $[[320,80,14]]$, $[[448,112,18]]$, and $[[2048,512,24]]$. All three have maximum check weight 10 on both the X and Z sides. Their canonical logical representatives have binary weights 25, 27, and 27, respectively, on both the X and Z sides.
summary: This paper presents a sophisticated algebraic method to construct complete canonical logical bases for qubit CSS quantum error-correcting codes derived from Pair-Partition codes. It utilizes quaternary coefficients and polynomial algebra to ensure the logical representatives span the entire logical space. The result provides explicit construction procedures and parameters for several high-performance quantum codes.
main_problem: The paper focuses on constructing complete canonical logical bases for qubit CSS quantum error-correcting codes.
main_result: A polynomial method using quaternary coefficients successfully constructs these canonical logical bases, yielding specific examples with high minimum distances.
method: The construction involves a multi-stage process: building initial binary checks, assigning quaternary coefficients ($\mathbb{F}_4$) to satisfy commutation relations, constructing logical matrices over $\mathbb{F}_4$, and finally expanding these into binary matrices.
model_or_system: The model is the qubit CSS code, defined by binary check matrices $H_X$ and $H_Z$. The construction is applied to Pair-Partition (PP) codes, utilizing circulant permutation matrices (CPMs) and algebraic techniques over polynomial rings.
key_observables: Code parameters $[[n, k, d]]$, check ranks, and the binary weights of the canonical logical representatives (e.g., 25, 27).
important_parameters: The construction is stated for general block dimensions ($J, L, P$), and examples include parameters like $[[320, 80, 14]]$ and $[[2048, 512, 24]]$.
main_assumptions: The method assumes the existence of invertible submatrices on disjoint column sets for the check systems, and it relies on the invertibility of a pairing polynomial $g(z)$.
figures_summary: The notes reference tables summarizing the parameters of seven constructed codes, detailing the resulting $[[n, k, d]]$ values and basis weights.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structured algebraic development: defining the problem (canonical bases), detailing the four stages of construction (initial checks, $\mathbb{F}_4$ assignment, $\mathbb{F}_4$ logical matrices, binary expansion), and concluding with specific examples and parameter reporting.
why_interesting: While highly abstract, the rigorous algebraic construction of error-correcting codes is foundational to quantum computation theory, providing concrete tools for designing fault-tolerant quantum hardware.
